extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages for a word prediction task, designed so that the target word is hard to guess from the last sentence alone but easy to guess with broader discourse context. It is intended as a benchmark for evaluating models' ability to understand broad context in natural language text.
extraction.creator: Denis Papemo, Germán Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bemardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Femández
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LAMBADA was built from the Book Corpus by taking passages from novels, after duplicate removal and filtering out potentially offensive material with a stop word list. The dataset was built from the development+testing partition, while models are intended to be trained on raw text from the separate training partition.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Book Corpus novels; after preprocessing, the corpus contained 5,325 novels and 465 million words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The task was to guess the last word of the target sentence (the target word). The context size was chosen in a pilot study, and the target word was constrained to be the last word of the sentence to make the task more natural for human subjects.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely over-represented in LAMBADA, while common nouns, verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are under-represented compared to the input distribution. The authors also note that more than 80% of LAMBADA passages include the target word in the context, which can make items strongly cued by broader discourse.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is a challenging benchmark for language modeling and is not representative of all text types; the authors note that broad context is needed for predictability and that many items can be guessed from local sentence context only. They also filtered out potentially offensive material, which may limit coverage of such content.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses minimizing the usefulness of external resources and notes filtering of potentially offensive material, but it does not provide a substantive broader social impact discussion.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset is drawn from novels and contains narrative text, but the paper does not state that it explicitly collects sensitive human attributes such as gender, age, socio-economic status, geography, language, culture, or experience.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and evaluating language modeling architectures on a word prediction task, with models trained on raw text from the training partition and evaluated on the development/testing partition.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list

name.evidence: We introduce LAMBADA, a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task.

description.evidence: LAMBADA is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
